p: Coventry has spent recent years reinventing itself, with its stint as UK City of Culture in 2021 bringing fresh attention to the place. The city has always had a creative, resilient streak, from its car-making heritage to its music scene, which gave the world the Two Tone sound and The Specials. A games bar fits that up-for-anything attitude nicely.

Coventry station is a short walk from the city centre, with direct trains to Birmingham and London, so it's well placed for a night out. If you're coming by car, the ring road wraps around the centre, with car parks dotted around it. It can be a bit confusing for first-timers, so sat-nav is your friend.

With two universities in the city, Coventry has a big student population, and that keeps the evenings lively, especially in term time. If you're out with a group of colleagues or friends who'd prefer a calmer evening, think about an earlier slot. If you're students looking for a big night, the later sessions will have the buzz you're after.

Want to make more of your visit? The Coventry Music Museum celebrates the city's Two Tone heritage and its many musical stories. The Belgrade Theatre has a long history of putting on shows, and the city's Canal Basin is a peaceful spot for a short walk. Warwick and Kenilworth, with their famous castles, are both a short drive away, so a day of history followed by an evening of games makes for a cracking weekend in the Midlands.
